bullets.title: ADP misses big: 98k jobs in June vs 118k est; wage growth flat
bullets.body: ADP's June employment report came in at 98k, well below the 118k Street estimate, with wage growth unchanged at 4.4%. Hiring was broad-based across firm sizes (small +53k, medium +29k, large +25k) but the headline miss signals a softening labor market, consistent with Conference Board consumer confidence falling to 91.2 in June with the labor market differential dropping to 2.4. Multiple sources note expectations for weaker labor prints through summer.

bullets.title: ISM Manufacturing 53.3 in June, misses; prices paid ease for second straight month
bullets.body: June ISM Manufacturing printed 53.3, below MS's 54.3 forecast and consensus 53.9, with production and new orders decelerating though remaining in expansion. Prices paid fell for the second consecutive month on easing energy prices, and supplier deliveries/inventories suggest improving supply constraints. Post-COVID manufacturing recovery continues to face headwinds from elevated protectionism.

bullets.title: Fed's Warsh tilts dovish, acknowledges falling inflation expectations; MS sees hold through YE26
bullets.body: Fed Chair Warsh declined to provide forward guidance on July but acknowledged inflation expectations have declined over the past four weeks and that inflation risks have come down — characterized as a dovish tilt despite efforts to avoid signaling. Morgan Stanley expects the Fed on hold through end of 2026, though UBS notes a significant minority of reserve managers see a pre-emptive July or September hike if US data stays strong.

bullets.title: AI capex share of GDP now exceeds 1990s tech boom; contribution to growth cooling
bullets.body: Analysis finds AI capex's contribution to final domestic demand is overstated by ~2/3 once semiconductor and hardware import drag is removed, and value-added growth from AI (particularly data processing) has recently cooled. Current AI capex as a share of GDP slightly exceeds the 1990s tech/telecom boom, raising overinvestment parallels; if spending merely stabilizes rather than contracts, aggregate demand hit is ~40bps — manageable. The case for a hawkish Fed driven by AI sector strength is now less clear.

bullets.title: Global PMIs soften: Foreign Mfg PMI -0.2pt to 51.5%; Japan Tankan surges but outlook weakens
bullets.body: PSC's preliminary June Foreign Manufacturing PMI slipped to 51.5% with both EM and DM ex-US aggregates declining; Taiwan and Korea PMIs slipped while Asia PMI overall eased to 51.6 (-0.3pp) from two-year highs, though 9 of 10 Asian economies remain in expansion. Japan's Large Manufacturing Tankan jumped to a cycle high of 22 (vs. 16 consensus), but the 3Q outlook component fell to 17, and All Industries Tankan is projected to slip to 11 in 3Q from 18. Eurozone June headline CPI came in below expectations at 2.8% y/y. Global growth forecast ticked down to 3.0% from 3.1%.

bullets.title: Momentum reversal risk: correlation at lows, semis/memory leading rotation; key levels SPX 7430, NVDA 190
bullets.body: Early session rotation out of momentum into laggards with memory, semis, and AI infrastructure leading weakness. COR1M correlation broke below 8 (to 5.79), a setup that historically precedes 10-20% momentum corrections and 2-3% S&P pullbacks — last similar setup preceded the June 5 unwind. Key technical levels: SPX 7500 resistance, gamma flip at 7430, DRAM 70 support, NVDA 190, SMH 575. JPM technical analysis separately flags the S&P stalling at 7617 with a potential dip to 7000-7200 as a buying opportunity, but warns a distribution pattern could form by Labor Day.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler vs. semiconductor divergence mirrors 1999-2000; JPM flags Q3-Q4 setoff risk
bullets.body: JPM technical strategy warns that hyperscalers (GOOGL, AMZN, MSFT, META, ORCL) underperforming semiconductors is creating a divergence analogous to the Communications Services vs. Equipment split in 1999-2000. If hyperscalers remain weak through summer, the setup could trigger a sentiment-driven setback into fall. Philly Semi maintains higher swing highs/lows but at a decelerated pace, with support at 11,760-12,870.

bullets.title: Semis broad premarket selloff: SNDK -4.7%, MU -3.3%, GLW -3.8%; memory/storage complex under pressure
bullets.body: Broad semiconductor and storage names sold off in premarket, led by SNDK -4.7%, GLW -3.8%, MU -3.3%, WDC -2.7%, COHR -2.3%, MRVL -2.1%, STX -2.0%, INTC -1.5%, AMD -1.4%. DRAM breaking below 70 support flagged as a key concern for sector confidence. S&P futures +0.18% at 7534.75; 10yr yield +4bps to 4.49%; WTI +0.85% to $68.91.

bullets.title: Market breadth broadening: small caps outperforming, Russell 2000 at historic relative lows vs S&P
bullets.body: Multiple sources highlight market leadership broadening beyond Mega-7, with small caps outperforming driven by improving earnings expectations and historical relative valuations near multi-decade lows vs. the S&P 500. Goldman notes June's S&P pullback masked broader strength with semis outperforming while Mag-7 declined ~7%; 2Q earnings expected to grow +22% YoY. 22V recommends an IWM Aug 290/260 put spread (~$4.60, 5.5x max payoff) as a near-term hedge ahead of mega-cap earnings, while remaining constructive longer-term with a Russell 2000 target of 3200.

bullets.title: IPO boom: $129B YTD (7x YoY), AI dominates; lockup expirations flagged as primary risk
bullets.body: US IPO volume hit $129B year-to-date, a 7x increase versus prior year, with the AI supercycle dominating institutional and retail appetite. Goldman notes current valuations are more disciplined than dot-com era with investors demanding real numbers, but flags twelve-figure lockup expirations as the primary risk if supply spikes and sentiment cools. Semiconductors are off to their best start to a year in 20+ years.

bullets.title: META launching 'Meta Compute' cloud business to monetize excess AI capacity; read mixed
bullets.body: Meta is building a cloud infrastructure business ('Meta Compute') to sell surplus AI computing capacity, potentially generating $10-15B annually. Citi notes early feedback is split on whether this signals overcapacity or a strategic monetization; MS Energy sees it as an 8% 2028 EPS upside 'backup safety valve.' The move also raises competitive questions for crypto miners using neoclouds.

bullets.title: GOOGL AI Overviews cut outbound clicks 40%, raise zero-click searches 35% — structural risk to web traffic
bullets.body: Citi analysis finds GOOGL's AI Overviews reduce outbound organic clicks by 39.8% and increase zero-click searches by 34.5% without improving user experience. This represents a structural headwind for publishers and ad-dependent businesses reliant on organic search traffic, while OpenAI has cut inference costs in half through optimization, accelerating competitive intensity.

bullets.title: BE +7.5% premarket: Brookfield partnership expands to $25B (25GW) on AI power demand
bullets.body: Bloom Energy expanded its Brookfield partnership from $5B to $25B, representing a 25GW capacity framework, with ~2.5GW already signed (AEP, ORCL, NBIS) and a path to 5GW+ by 2030. OKLO also gained (+3.4-3.9%) after DOE approved the final safety analysis for its Groves Isotope Test Reactor, targeting first criticality in July 2026. Power prices surged at major US hubs (PJM Western Hub $342 vs. $117 prior).

bullets.title: Asia equity: MSCI APAC -1.1% in June; China -7.1%, Taiwan +1.4% on AI; Korea cheapest at 7.3x FTM PE
bullets.body: MSCI Asia Pacific fell 1.1% in June with China MSCI down 7.1% on domestic economic softness and weak offshore internet, while Taiwan (+1.4%) and Korea (+0.1%) outperformed on AI infrastructure strength. DXY rose 2.3%, oil fell 20.8%, and gold dropped 11.7%, with the US 10yr at 4.46%. Korea trades at the lowest regional forward PE of 7.3x; Taiwan is expensive at +3.1 standard deviations above historical mean. Foreign investors exited Asia for a fourth consecutive month in India.

bullets.title: Retail traffic decelerating: Q2 +1.7% vs Q1 +3.4%; consumer confidence softer, labor differential falling
bullets.body: Citi's retail traffic tracker shows Q2 deceleration to +1.7% (ex-Walmart +1.9%) versus +3.4% in Q1, with June week 4 at +2.3% vs +5.4% in week 3 partly due to Father's Day timing. Strongest names: Five +18.3%, Ross +17.3%; weakest: RL -12.2%, AEO -10.5%, Gap -3.9%. Conference Board consumer confidence hit 91.2 in June with the labor market differential falling to 2.4, signaling potential for weaker labor data through summer.

bullets.title: Guggenheim upgrades CRM and NOW to Buy; AI risk manageable, valuations imply perpetual decline
bullets.body: Guggenheim upgraded CRM (Buy, $228 PT) and NOW (Buy, $125 PT), arguing current valuations price in a perpetual decline scenario that Guggenheim views as overstated. The firm expects AI will materially impact software but most names will persist, with subscription revenue growth stabilizing this year and potentially accelerating in late 2026 and into 2027. Both stocks responded: CRM +4.1% and NOW +4.6% in premarket.

bullets.title: Redbook retail +10.5% YoY; agentic commerce emerging with AMZN best-in-class at 77% recommendation rate
bullets.body: Redbook retail sales accelerated to +10.5% YoY, supporting a constructive consumer backdrop despite deceleration in tracked foot traffic. DA Davidson's agentic commerce testing shows AMZN achieved a 77% recommendation rate across 35 project-based queries, best-in-class; Amazon also launched Alexa for Shopping with 30/90/365-day price history. 64% of UK consumers expressed interest in AI shopping agents.

bullets.title: REITs +18% YTD, outperforming S&P +10%; datacenter REIT exposure expanding
bullets.body: REITs have returned +18% YTD on a total return basis versus S&P +10%, with Realty Income announcing a JV to invest in hyperscale datacenters under long-term triple-net leases. The datacenter/power nexus continues to attract REIT capital as a structural theme.

bullets.title: Eurozone CPI below expectations at 2.8% y/y; ECB 'no-regret hike' seen as well-positioned
bullets.body: Euro area flash CPI came in mild at -0.1% m/m and 2.8% y/y, below expectations, aided by energy backdrop (12-month Brent ~$72/bbl). UBS characterizes the ECB's recent hike as a 'no-regret' move leaving the bank well-positioned with medium-term inflation near target. European corporates remain resilient to the energy shock but show no acceleration, with gradual AI spend increases pressuring margins.

bullets.title: Steeper yield curve, improving loan growth boosting regional bank earnings power; USB and FITB preferred
bullets.body: 22V highlights steeper yield curve as a tailwind for bank NII, with loan growth continuing to exceed investor expectations and deposit pricing remaining disciplined. USB and FITB are preferred picks on improving NII, loan growth, and fee trends. The labor market is seen as gradually strengthening rather than overheating, supporting a benign credit backdrop.
